name: Hospitals (Medicare-certified)
plain: How many hospitals that Medicare certifies are in each municipality.
definition: Hospitals in CMS's Hospital General Information list, counted in the municipality of the hospital: acute care, psychiatric, children's and the VA hospital. Hospitals that do not take part in Medicare are not in the list.
geography: 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico (the island value is the sum of the 78 municipal values)

coverage.frequency: One snapshot, made from the CMS lists of 2026-10-14. It is rebuilt with each full build (python care_series.py).

method: care_series.py reads the Puerto Rico rows of the CMS list through the Provider Data Catalog API and counts them in the municipality the row's county field names (for home health agencies, the town field; four towns named by a barrio or sector are placed by their ZIP code). A name that is not a municipality stops the build. Names, addresses, telephone numbers and certification numbers are never kept or published.
source_detail: CMS Provider Data Catalog API, datastore/query/{dataset}/0 with state = PR
how_to_read: Puerto Rico has 59 such hospitals in 24 municipalities; most are in San Juan 20, Bayamón 5, Ponce 4.
caveats: A hospital is counted once, where it is, whatever its size.
Hospitals outside Medicare are not counted.

name: Road distance to the nearest health center (average per resident, km)
plain: On average, how far residents of each municipality live from the nearest community health center, along the roads.
definition: The road distance from where each resident lives (the 2020 census block) to the nearest permanent health center site, averaged over the municipality's residents, in kilometres.
geography: 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico (each an average over its residents)

coverage.frequency: One estimate, from HRSA's site list of 2026-10-14 and the 2020 census blocks. Rebuilt with each full build.

method: care_access.py, run by care_series.py, searches the observatory's road graph (site/data/roads.bin, from OpenStreetMap) from every permanent health center site of HRSA's list at once, in both directions of every road, and measures from each 2020 census block with residents (its internal point, snapped to the nearest road that is joined to the network within 2 km) to the nearest site. A municipality's value is the average over its residents (each block weighted by its 2020 residents). The site points come from HRSA's file and stay in the local cache only (owner decision, 2026-10-14); they are never published. In the 2026-10 run, 124 sites, 36,570 blocks; 3 blocks (46 residents) have no road within 2 km and are left out.
source_detail: HRSA Health Center Service Delivery and Look-Alike Sites (Geocoding Artifact Address Primary X and Y Coordinate, used in the build only); 2020 census blocks (network.py); OpenStreetMap roads (roads.py)
how_to_read: Puerto Rico's residents live on average 5.13 km by road from the nearest health center. The longest averages are in Villalba 20.1 km, Sabana Grande 13.9 km, Juana Díaz 13.7 km; the shortest in Culebra 2.4 km, Arroyo 2.5 km, Florida 2.5 km.
caveats: It is the distance to the nearest health center (a federally funded community health center or look-alike), not to a hospital, an emergency department or a doctor's office.
It says nothing about hours, services, waiting times or whether the center takes a person's insurance.
An estimate made by the observatory, not a figure HRSA publishes.

HRSA's site list of 2026-10-14, which this estimate uses, has no permanent site in Villalba or Las Marías, while the counts of health center sites (health.hc_sites, from HRSA's file of 2026-10-06) still show one in each: the two lists are a week apart, and both are HRSA's as published.

view.label: Map, Analysis tab: road distance to the nearest health center (average per resident, km)
